theory.intro: Raw results from different tests can be misleading when their means and spreads differ. Standardising each result puts it on a common scale. For marks, where higher is better, the **higher** $z$-score is the better relative result. Decide which direction is better in the context.
facts: Calculate a $z$-score for each result with $z = \dfrac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$ before comparing them.
When a higher value is better, the result with the higher $z$-score is better relative to its own group.
A lower raw score can win, because a small mark in a hard test can still sit further above its own mean.
Compare signed numbers: for marks where higher is better, $-0.4$ is better than $-1.2$.
When a **low** value is better, such as a race time or a golf score, the more negative $z$-score is the better result.
When the same direction is better in both contexts, equal $z$-scores represent equivalent performance relative to the groups.
State the conclusion in context and quote both $z$-scores as the justification.
steps: Calculate the z-score for each result
Decide which direction is better in this context
Compare the z-scores and state the conclusion

workedExamples.question_text:
The table shows a student's marks and the class mean and standard deviation.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Subject}&\text{Mark}&\mu&\sigma\\\hline\text{English}&69&63&7\\\text{History}&41&47&8\\\text{Science}&73&66&9\end{array}$
(a) Calculate each $z$-score, correct to $2$ decimal places.
(b) In which subject was the relative performance best, and in which was it worst? Justify your answers.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Use $z=\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$.
English: $z=\dfrac{69-63}{7}=0.857142\ldots\approx0.86$.
History: $z=\dfrac{41-47}{8}=-0.75$.
Science: $z=\dfrac{73-66}{9}=0.777777\ldots\approx0.78$.
(b) Higher marks are better, so compare the signed $z$-scores from highest to lowest.
$0.857142\ldots>0.777777\ldots>-0.75$.
The relative performance was best in English and worst in History. Science has the highest raw mark, but English has the highest standardised score.

workedExamples.question_text:
A swimmer completes freestyle in $49.4$ s, where the club mean is $53.1$ s and the standard deviation is $2.3$ s. The swimmer completes backstroke in $62.7$ s, where the club mean is $67.9$ s and the standard deviation is $3.6$ s.
Calculate both $z$-scores, correct to $2$ decimal places, and decide which swim was better relative to the club. A lower time is better.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Freestyle: $z=\dfrac{49.4-53.1}{2.3}$
$=-1.608695\ldots\approx-1.61$.
Backstroke: $z=\dfrac{62.7-67.9}{3.6}$
$=-1.444444\ldots\approx-1.44$.
Lower times are better here, so the more negative $z$-score is better.
$-1.608695\ldots<-1.444444\ldots$.
The freestyle swim was better relative to the club. Comparing only the seconds below each mean would give the wrong choice.

workedExamples.question_text:
A student scores $74$ in English, where the mean is $68$ and the standard deviation is $7$. The student's performance is to be equivalent in each other test.
(a) What mark is needed in Maths, where the mean is $61$ and the standard deviation is $9.5$?
(b) In Art the student scores $72$, and the standard deviation is $8.5$. Find the mean for Art.
Give the mark and mean correct to $1$ decimal place.
workedExamples.solution_text:
English: $z=\dfrac{74-68}{7}=\dfrac67$.
Keep this exact score for both parts.
(a) Equivalent performance needs the same $z$-score.
$x=\mu+z\sigma$
$=61+\dfrac67\times9.5$
$=69.142857\ldots\approx69.1$.
(b) Use the same score in Art.
$\dfrac67=\dfrac{72-\mu}{8.5}$
$\dfrac67\times8.5=72-\mu$
$\mu=72-\dfrac67\times8.5$
$=64.714285\ldots\approx64.7$.

foundation.question_text:
Hana scored $74$ in History, where the mean was $68$ and the standard deviation was $8$.
She scored $66$ in Geography, where the mean was $60$ and the standard deviation was $6$.
In which subject was her result better relative to the rest of the class?
Justify your answer.
foundation.solution_text:
History: $z = \dfrac{74 - 68}{8}$
$= 0.75$
Geography: $z = \dfrac{66 - 60}{6}$
$= 1$
$1 > 0.75$, so her Geography result was better relative to the class, even though her History mark was the higher one.

foundation.question_text:
Marco scored $46$ in Music, where the mean was $50$ and the standard deviation was $10$.
He scored $33$ in Drama, where the mean was $37$ and the standard deviation was $5$.
In which subject was his result better relative to the rest of the class?
Justify your answer.
foundation.solution_text:
Music: $z = \dfrac{46 - 50}{10}$
$= -0.4$
Drama: $z = \dfrac{33 - 37}{5}$
$= -0.8$
Both results are below the mean, but $-0.4 > -0.8$, so his Music result was better relative to the class.

foundation.question_text:
Sione swims $100$ m freestyle in $62$ seconds, where the club mean is $68$ seconds with a standard deviation of $3$ seconds.
He swims $100$ m backstroke in $75$ seconds, where the club mean is $82$ seconds with a standard deviation of $4$ seconds.
A faster (lower) time is better.
In which event is his swim better relative to the club?
Justify your answer.
foundation.solution_text:
Freestyle: $z = \dfrac{62 - 68}{3}$
$= -2$
Backstroke: $z = \dfrac{75 - 82}{4}$
$= -1.75$
A lower time is better here, so the more negative $z$-score is the better result.
$-2 < -1.75$, so his freestyle swim is better relative to the club.

foundation.question_text:
The table shows Amira's marks in three subjects, with the class mean and standard deviation for each.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} \text{Subject} & \text{Mark} & \mu & \sigma \\ \hline \text{English} & 62 & 58 & 5 \\ \text{Maths} & 71 & 65 & 12 \\ \text{Science} & 55 & 52 & 4 \end{array}$
In which subject was her relative performance the best?
Justify your answer.
foundation.solution_text:
English: $z = \dfrac{62 - 58}{5}$
$= 0.8$
Maths: $z = \dfrac{71 - 65}{12}$
$= 0.5$
Science: $z = \dfrac{55 - 52}{4}$
$= 0.75$
$0.8$ is the highest of the three $z$-scores, so her relative performance was best in English, even though Maths was her highest mark.

foundation.question_text:
Nina scored $72$ in Art, where the mean was $60$ and the standard deviation was $8$.
What mark in Music, where the mean was $54$ and the standard deviation was $6$, would represent an equivalent performance?
foundation.solution_text:
Art: $z = \dfrac{72 - 60}{8}$
$= 1.5$
An equivalent performance in Music needs the same $z$-score.
$x = \mu + z\sigma$
$= 54 + 1.5 \times 6$
$= 54 + 9$
$= 63$

foundation.question_text:
Owen scored $68$ in Physics, where the mean was $62$ and the standard deviation was $4$.
He scored $79$ in Chemistry, where the mean was $70$ and the standard deviation was $9$.
Owen claims Chemistry was his stronger result.
Is he correct?
Justify your answer.
foundation.solution_text:
Physics: $z = \dfrac{68 - 62}{4}$
$= 1.5$
Chemistry: $z = \dfrac{79 - 70}{9}$
$= 1$
$1.5 > 1$, so Physics was his stronger result relative to the class.
Owen is not correct; his higher Chemistry mark came in a test where the marks were more spread out.

development.question_text:

Give both $z$-scores correct to two decimal places.
development.solution_text:

$= 1.2307...$
$\approx 1.23$
Legal Studies: $z = \dfrac{64 - 58}{4.8}$

development.question_text:
Gina plays two rounds of golf on different courses.
On the first course she scores $78$, where the mean score is $84$ with a standard deviation of $5$.
On the second course she scores $82$, where the mean score is $91$ with a standard deviation of $6$.
In golf a lower score is better.
On which course was her round better relative to the other players?
Justify your answer.
development.solution_text:
First course: $z = \dfrac{78 - 84}{5}$
$= -1.2$
Second course: $z = \dfrac{82 - 91}{6}$
$= -1.5$
A lower score is better here, so the more negative $z$-score is the better round.
$-1.5 < -1.2$, so her round on the second course was better, even though $82$ is the higher score.

development.question_text:
The table shows Jae's marks in four subjects, with the class mean and standard deviation for each.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} \text{Subject} & \text{Mark} & \mu & \sigma \\ \hline \text{Biology} & 66 & 58 & 8 \\ \text{Chemistry} & 54 & 60 & 8 \\ \text{PE} & 81 & 72 & 12 \\ \text{Maths} & 48 & 55 & 10 \end{array}$
In which subject was his relative performance the best, and in which was it the worst?
Justify your answers.
development.solution_text:
Biology: $z = \dfrac{66 - 58}{8} = 1$
Chemistry: $z = \dfrac{54 - 60}{8} = -0.75$
PE: $z = \dfrac{81 - 72}{12} = 0.75$
Maths: $z = \dfrac{48 - 55}{10} = -0.7$
The highest $z$-score is $1$, so his relative performance was best in Biology.
The lowest $z$-score is $-0.75$, and $-0.75 < -0.7$, so his relative performance was worst in Chemistry.

development.question_text:
Zoe scored $47$ in Japanese, where the mean was $53$ and the standard deviation was $10$.
What mark in French, where the mean was $61$ and the standard deviation was $7.5$, would represent an equivalent performance?
development.solution_text:
Japanese: $z = \dfrac{47 - 53}{10}$
$= -0.6$
An equivalent performance in French needs the same $z$-score.
$x = \mu + z\sigma$
$= 61 + (-0.6) \times 7.5$
$= 61 - 4.5$
$= 56.5$

development.question_text:
Ravi scored $63$ in Test 1, where the mean was $57$ and the standard deviation was $8$.
He scored $78$ in Test 2, where the mean was $66$ and the standard deviation was $16$.
Ravi says his performance relative to the class improved from Test 1 to Test 2.
Is he correct?
Justify your answer.
development.solution_text:
Test 1: $z = \dfrac{63 - 57}{8}$
$= 0.75$
Test 2: $z = \dfrac{78 - 66}{16}$
$= 0.75$
The two $z$-scores are equal, so his position relative to the class is unchanged.
Ravi is not correct; his mark rose by $15$, but the class mean and the spread rose with it.

development.question_text:
Kiri scored $48$ in Maths, where the mean was $55$ and the standard deviation was $7$.
She scored $61$ in Music, where the mean was $58$ and the standard deviation was $6$.
In which subject was her result better relative to the class?
Justify your answer.
development.solution_text:
Maths: $z = \dfrac{48 - 55}{7}$
$= -1$
Music: $z = \dfrac{61 - 58}{6}$
$= 0.5$
Her Maths result is below the mean and her Music result is above it.
$0.5 > -1$, so her Music result was better relative to the class.

mastery.question_text:
The table shows Layla's marks in five subjects, with the class mean and standard deviation for each.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} \text{Subject} & \text{Mark} & \mu & \sigma \\ \hline \text{English} & 68 & 62 & 8 \\ \text{Maths} & 55 & 61 & 12 \\ \text{Biology} & 79 & 70 & 6 \\ \text{History} & 64 & 64 & 9 \\ \text{PE} & 72 & 60 & 15 \end{array}$
Rank the five subjects from her best relative performance to her worst.
mastery.solution_text:
English: $z = \dfrac{68 - 62}{8} = 0.75$
Maths: $z = \dfrac{55 - 61}{12} = -0.5$
Biology: $z = \dfrac{79 - 70}{6} = 1.5$
History: $z = \dfrac{64 - 64}{9} = 0$
PE: $z = \dfrac{72 - 60}{15} = 0.8$
Ordering the $z$-scores from highest to lowest gives $1.5$, $0.8$, $0.75$, $0$, $-0.5$.
Best to worst: Biology, PE, English, History, Maths.

mastery.question_text:
Priya's standardised score was the same in Music and in Art.
In Music she scored $71$, where the mean was $59$ and the standard deviation was $8$.
In Art she scored $80$, where the standard deviation was $12$.
Find the mean mark for Art.
mastery.solution_text:
Music: $z = \dfrac{71 - 59}{8}$
$= 1.5$
Her Art $z$-score is also $1.5$.
$\mu = x - z\sigma$
$= 80 - 1.5 \times 12$
$= 80 - 18$
$= 62$

mastery.question_text:
Ben runs $800$ m in $2$ minutes $14$ seconds, where his club's mean is $2$ minutes $26$ seconds with a standard deviation of $8$ seconds.
Cody runs $1500$ m in $4$ minutes $52$ seconds, where his club's mean is $5$ minutes $10$ seconds with a standard deviation of $15$ seconds.
A faster (lower) time is better.
Which runner performed better relative to his own club?
Justify your answer.
mastery.solution_text:
Work in seconds throughout.
Ben: $z = \dfrac{134 - 146}{8}$
$= \dfrac{-12}{8}$
$= -1.5$
Cody: $z = \dfrac{292 - 310}{15}$
$= \dfrac{-18}{15}$
$= -1.2$
A lower time is better here, so the more negative $z$-score is the better run.
$-1.5 < -1.2$, so Ben performed better relative to his own club.
